title: MIPIM Cannes Global Summit 2026
label: Press Briefing
pressBriefing: The Cannes Summit concluded with a clear consensus: institutional capital is resuming active underwriting, but the underwriting criteria has structurally pivoted toward governance and execution history rather than speculative far-land banks.
Our team reported live from the Carlton, charting key conversations with major private equity sponsors and municipal developers.
keyTakeaways: Sovereign funds are pricing in a longer cost-of-capital cycle, rewarding sponsors with governance over asset scale.
Green premiums are no longer optional additions; they are key underwriting baselines for European and Asian pension pools.
Mixed-use vertical urbanism is capturing the highest secondary yield resilience across Tier-1 global transit cities.

title: Roundtable: Distressed Assets and Re-capitalization
label: Press Briefing
pressBriefing: A select closed-door roundtable of lenders, asset reconstruction firms, and capital sponsors convened to assess distressed asset absorption corridors. We tracked key insights on Far resolution timelines and liquidity exit paths.
In contrast to public marketing narratives, deep balance-sheet restructurings are requiring significant FAR modifications and pricing corrections before secondary entry.
keyTakeaways: Asset reconstruction companies are increasingly demanding active FAR adjustments from municipal regulators to achieve viability.
Exit spreads are narrowing as secondary retail platforms selectively acquire only Grade-A distress chunks.
Title sequence resolution continues to be the single biggest bottleneck, extending restructurings by 18-24 months.

title: Symposium: High-Street Retail Dynamics
label: Press Briefing
pressBriefing: The Symposium explored the remarkable divergence between large mall performance indices and emerging high-street strata assets. Strata-ownership models are reshaping investment options, but retail lease discipline remains highly fragmented.
Our report outlines why brand anchor retention and maintenance sequencing are deciding pricing power.
keyTakeaways: High streets are experiencing a sharp yield spike, but replacement leasing risks are higher due to fragmented strata-ownership.
Brands are increasingly insisting on anchor-rent structures tied to localized footfall and revenue share indices.
Institutional mall operators are successfully counter-acting high-street competition by consolidating entertainment space.
